correctness.rationale: Every source vertex has equally many selected U and D coordinates, and direct exact expansion makes its squared distance from \(c_lpha\) equal to \(pq/m\), independent of the matching. For any finite common-sphere point set, projection of the sphere center onto the convex hull gives an enclosing ball of squared radius \(R_0^2-d^2\), while the projection face supplies a convex contact certificate proving optimality and uniqueness. The source H-description and its all-prefix consequence make \(c_lpha\) feasible exactly when every normalized prefix discrepancy lies in \([0,1]\).

value.rationale: Shard polytopes are Minkowski-indecomposable building blocks for quotientopes and have a nontrivial series-parallel matroid interpretation. The theorem adds a complete Euclidean boundary phenomenon: all shard vertices always share an explicit sphere, but the arc word decides whether that sphere is actually minimal through a sharp prefix strip. The equivalent uniform-density criterion links a geometric radius question to a natural matroid density property, while the projection formula still gives the exact true radius when balance fails.
